subject: Chemistry
central_question: How do carbon–carbon bond type and electron delocalisation determine the structure, preparation, reactions, and uses of hydrocarbons?
in_scope_units: Alkanes: preparation, properties, reactions, and conformations.
Alkenes: geometry, isomerism, electrophilic addition, ozonolysis, and polymerisation.
Alkynes: structure, acidity, preparation, and reactions.
Benzene: aromaticity, preparation, electrophilic substitution, directing effects, and toxicity.

known_pitfalls.correction: They undergo substitution, combustion, oxidation, and aromatisation under suitable conditions.

known_pitfalls.claim: Markovnikov rule applies to every addition.
known_pitfalls.correction: It applies to suitable unsymmetrical additions; peroxide changes HBr orientation.
Only terminal alkynes contain that hydrogen.

known_pitfalls.claim: Benzene reacts like an ordinary alkene.
known_pitfalls.correction: Aromatic delocalisation makes substitution strongly preferred.

ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use exercises on nomenclature, isomerism, chlorination, conformations, addition reactions, Markovnikov orientation, ozonolysis, benzene substitution, directing effects, and toxicity.
